iut_type: End Product (Topre keyboard, RC1/R4H series), adding a new HID keycode to an already-certified device
customer_question: For an already Bluetooth-certified keyboard, if we add a new keycode to what's sent over Bluetooth (for example, adding a Mute key when we'd previously only registered Vol Up/Down among the multimedia keys, with the Report Descriptor for multimedia keys already in place), do we need to re-apply for certification?
question_variants: Does adding a new HID keycode trigger a re-certification requirement?
What if the keycode addition comes with a new model name?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to add a new keyboard key function (Mute) to the set of keycodes their already-certified keyboard could send over Bluetooth, and needed to know whether this kind of incremental keycode addition would require going through certification again.
plain_english_explanation: The existing registration's content doesn't include any information that limits which specific keys or keycodes the device is allowed to send — so adding a new keycode (like Mute) to the existing multimedia-key Report Descriptor doesn't require re-application at all. The only scenario requiring action is if the keycode addition is accompanied by an entirely new model name being issued for the product — in that case, the new model should be added via the standard 'Qualify Additional Products' button on the Product List page, treating it as a routine derivative-model addition rather than a full new certification.
consultant_answer: No re-application is needed — your existing registration doesn't include any information limiting which specific keycodes can be sent, so adding a new keycode like Mute to your existing multimedia-key Report Descriptor doesn't require re-certification. The only action needed is if this change comes with an entirely new model name — in that case, just add the new model via the 'Qualify Additional Products' button on your Product List page, as a routine derivative-model addition.
decision_logic: Adding a keycode within an already-registered HID function category (like multimedia keys) doesn't trigger re-certification, since the registration doesn't constrain specific key assignments — only a new model name issuance requires a (free, routine) derivative-model addition action.
final_recommendation: When a customer asks about incremental HID keycode additions to an already-certified keyboard, confirm that registration content doesn't typically constrain specific key assignments, and clarify that only a new model name (not the keycode change itself) would trigger any registration action.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer mistakenly believing every keycode addition requires full re-certification could incur unnecessary cost and delay for routine product feature additions that don't actually affect their registration's validity.
